2027-01-18.title: Third Monday of Denha · First Day of the Three Days' Fast
2027-01-18.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: God, the LORD, is my strength
Forgive your brother or sister from your heart
2027-01-18.alt: Season of Denha. Three Days' Fast (Moonnu Nombu, the Rogation of the Ninevites). Church Unity Octave begins (Ephesians 4:1–6; John 17:6–11).
2027-01-18.verse: Yet, O LORD, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand.
theo: Today begins the Three Days' Fast, the Rogation of the Ninevites, born in a time of plague when the Church of the East fasted and begged God for mercy. The first reading gives us the words for such a prayer. A people back from exile looks at its ruins and cries: “O that you would tear open the heavens and come down”. They do not pretend: “all our righteous deeds are like a filthy cloth. We all fade like a leaf”. Yet they hold on to one truth: “Yet, O LORD, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter”, and they plead: “do not remember iniquity forever. Now consider, we are all your people.” Habakkuk adds the faith that keeps praying even when the fields are bare: “Though the fig tree does not blossom… yet I will rejoice in the LORD”.

Paul urges that “supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for everyone”, even for kings and rulers, because God “desires everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.” A rogation is exactly this: the Church praying for the whole world. But Jesus warns that a prayer for mercy is empty if we refuse mercy. The servant released from a debt of ten thousand talents seizes a fellow servant by the throat over a hundred denarii. The master asks: “Should you not have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I had mercy on you?” And Jesus says the Father will deal so with us “if you do not forgive your brother or sister from your heart.” Our fast begins with forgiveness. Today the Unity Octave also begins: Christians who ask God not to remember their sins must learn to forgive one another.
outline: Ask: what would you say to God if you saw your town in ruins?
Isaiah's honest prayer: you are our Father.
God desires all to be saved.
The servant forgiven much who would not forgive little.
“Yet, O LORD, you are our Father.”
live: Keep the fast today as your health allows: one simple meal, no snacks, no meat.
Name one person you have not forgiven and forgive him or her from your heart today, in prayer and, if possible, in deed.
2027-01-18.prayer: Merciful Father, we are the clay and you are our potter. As we begin the fast of the Ninevites, do not remember our iniquity forever. Teach us to pray for everyone, and give us hearts that forgive as we have been forgiven. Make all Christians one in your mercy. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the Church prays for the whole world, for rulers and for all peoples, as Paul asks; and we approach the altar only after forgiving our brother and sister.

quick: We are the clay; God is our Father and potter.
Pray for everyone; God desires all to be saved.
Forgive from the heart as you have been forgiven.
2027-01-18.action: Keep today's fast and forgive one person from your heart.
2027-01-18.question: Whom do I still hold by the throat over a small debt?

family.explain: A king forgave a servant a huge debt. But that servant would not forgive a friend who owed him a little. Jesus says: God has forgiven us so much, so we must forgive others.
family.intention: We pray for our country, our leaders and the whole world, as St Paul asks.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone in our family we need to forgive today?”

illus: Two brothers near Pala had not spoken for nine years over a strip of rubber land. On the first morning of Moonnu Nombu the younger one heard the parable of the unforgiving servant at Qurbana. That evening he walked to his brother's gate with the land papers and said: keep it; I want my brother more than the land. Their mother said it was the best fast the family had ever kept.

pm.open: Merciful Father, as we begin the fast of the Ninevites, shape us like clay in your hands and teach us to forgive. Amen.
share: We are the clay, and you are our potter (Isaiah 64:8). Do I let God reshape me?
Prayers for everyone (1 Timothy 2:1). Whom do I forget to pray for?
Forgive your brother or sister from your heart (Matthew 18:35). Whom must I forgive?
interc: For the Church, that these three days may bring true conversion.
For rulers and all in authority, as St Paul asks.
For those who carry grudges and those who cannot forgive.
For our group, that our fasting may make us merciful.
pm.close: Lord God, you are our Father and we are the work of your hand. Forgive us as we forgive, and renew us through prayer and fasting. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today we begin the Three Days' Fast, the fast of the Ninevites. Our Church of the East first kept it in a time of plague, when the people fasted and begged God for mercy. The first reading gives us the words for that prayer.

A people back from exile looks at its ruins and cries: O that you would tear open the heavens and come down! They confess: all our righteous deeds are like a filthy cloth; we all fade like a leaf. Then comes the turn: yet, O LORD, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter (Isaiah 64:8). A broken pot can be remade if it stays in the potter's hands.

Habakkuk teaches us to rejoice in God even when the fig tree does not blossom and the fields yield no food. And Paul asks that prayers be made for everyone, for kings and all in authority, because God desires everyone to be saved (1 Timothy 2:4). A rogation is the whole Church praying for the whole world.

But Jesus tells a hard parable. A servant is forgiven a debt he could never pay, then throttles a fellow servant over a small sum. The master asks: should you not have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I had mercy on you? (Matthew 18:33). If we ask God not to remember our sins, we cannot keep a list of the sins of others.
Today the Church Unity Octave also begins. Let our fast begin with forgiveness: in our families, in our parishes, and among divided Christians. Amen.
kids: Children, a king forgave a man a huge debt, but the man would not forgive his friend a tiny one. Jesus wants us to forgive like God forgives us. Is there someone you need to say sorry to, or forgive, today?

intro: Theme: “Yet, O LORD, you are our Father.”
The fast of the Ninevites begins: prayer for mercy, prayer for all, mercy to one another.

q: Yet, O LORD, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand.
But we have this treasure in clay jars, so that it may be made clear that this extraordinary power belongs to God and does not come from us.
points.apply: Keep the three days' fast as fully as you can, as clay in God's hands.

sub: God desires all to be saved.
q: But seek the welfare of the city where I have sent you into exile, and pray to the LORD on its behalf, for in its welfare you will find your welfare.
This is right and is acceptable in the sight of God our Savior, who desires everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
points.apply: Pray each day of the fast for our country and its leaders.

q: Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done, and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray.
Should you not have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I had mercy on you?
points.apply: Forgive one person from your heart before the fast ends.

concl: The rogation of the Ninevites is a prayer for mercy for all.
We who ask mercy must give mercy.
2027-01-18.resolve: Make a good confession during the three days, and forgive before you confess.
